subject: Post-demo: ACME model shortlist & tradeoffs
messages:

Subject: Post-demo recap + next steps

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciate the time, Jordan (and Priya on your side). Quick recap and agreed next steps from our call: 

- Goals: reduce user-facing latency to <= 350ms p95 for chat completions, keep inference cost under $0.002 / 1k tokens, and maintain current quality for your product prompts (few-shot QA + retrieval-augmented responses).
- Constraints: on-device/regional hosting is not required initially; data residency for EU users will be a future ask.
- Action items: Redwood to send a recommended model shortlist with cost/latency/quality tradeoffs + a small prompt set for evaluation. ACME to share any additional evaluation prompts and confirm priority KPIs.

I'll follow up tomorrow with the shortlist and a benchmark file you can run locally or review in the Drive link. If the timing looks good, can we tentatively block 30 mins next week to walk through the results?

Attachments: none in this message (shortlist and bench to follow).

Thanks Marissa — that recap looks right. Couple of clarifying points before you send the shortlist: 

1) Quality baseline: our current in-house model scores ~0.78 on our internal QA F1 across the prompt suite; we evaluate hallucination separately and prefer precision over recall for customer-facing answers.
2) Cost target: $0.0015–$0.002 per 1k tokens is ideal; we can stretch slightly for a noticeable quality uplift.
3) Latency SLO: 350ms p95 is the target; 250ms would be fantastic but not required.

Also, we'll attach our evaluation prompt set if that helps — Priya will drop it in this thread. Looking forward to the shortlist so we can start A/Bing quickly.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme.com>, Priya Desai <priya@acme.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps — recommended model shortlist + benchmarks

Hi Jordan & Priya — attaching a concise recommended shortlist and the benchmark/pass-fail prompt set for your quick evals. Summary below; full numbers and raw logs are in acme_model_benchmarks.csv (attached) and the Drive link. 

Recommended shortlist (recommended order = our suggested pilot path):

1) LlamaX-13B-quant (2-bit) — Low cost, low latency (est. $0.0009 / 1k tokens; p95 ~220–280ms on our Dedicated NVLink pool). Quality: good for retrieval-augmented QA with your prompt set; minimal regression risk if evaluated on the provided prompt set. Best for aggressive cost-first pilots.

2) Redstone-33B (int8) — Mid cost, balanced latency (est. $0.0018 / 1k tokens; p95 ~300–360ms). Quality: stronger out-of-the-box reasoning and fewer hallucinations on closed-domain content. Good middle-ground when quality matters and cost flexibility exists.

3) OpenLambda-70B (fp16) — Higher cost, higher latency (est. $0.0045 / 1k tokens; p95 ~420–520ms). Quality: top-tier for complex multi-step reasoning; recommend only if clear quality delta is required and you can accept higher cost/latency or use a selective routing strategy (e.g., heavy prompts route to 70B, others to 13B).

Engineering notes and tradeoffs:
- Cost numbers are per-token inference estimates; they assume Redwood Dedicated execution with autoscaling and standard batching.
- Latency p95 is measured on our benchmark harness with 90–300 token outputs; we include continuous batching overhead in the numbers.
- Regression risks: quantized variants (LlamaX-13B-quant) can show small accuracy drops on edge-case prompts. We recommend running the attached prompt set and our provided eval harness to flag regressions before rollout.

Attached: acme_model_benchmarks.csv (detailed per-prompt metrics), practical_prompt_set.txt (30 prioritized prompts we used in the benchmark). Drive link (full logs & eval harness): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ACMEExampleSharedDrive

Next steps I suggest: 
- You run the attached prompt set and share any additional priority prompts by Tue EOD.
- We'll provision a short Dedicated pilot environment for ACME, load the three model variants, and run a 48-hour live evaluation against your traffic profile.
- Sync: 30-min follow-up next Thu — propose Thu 12pm PT; I can send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Let me know if you'd like us to include cost-sensitivity knobs (dynamic batching/kv caching) or to pre-configure a selective routing policy for hybrid usage.

Attachments: acme_model_benchmarks.csv, practical_prompt_set.txt

Marissa Cole

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps — recommended model shortlist + benchmarks

Quick engineering notes to flag before we send the Dedicated pilot details to ACME: 

- For LlamaX-13B-quant: recommend running both 2-bit and 4-bit quant runs in the pilot. 2-bit gives the cost wins you listed but 4-bit sometimes preserves quality for edge cases; include both configs in the 48-hour run and compare per-prompt regressions.
- For Redstone-33B int8: we should test with and without KV cache warmup to measure cold-start behavior; ACME's user flows include many short sessions which can exaggerate cold penalty.
- For routing: if we propose selective routing to OpenLambda-70B for heavy prompts, provide an explicit fallback to Redstone-33B to avoid p95 blowups during spikes.
- Eval harness: we'll instrument a quick regression monitor (per-prompt diff + hallucination score) and report daily; Marissa, please share ACME's privacy/data retention constraints so we can configure logs retention appropriately.

I'll prepare the pilot config and send a short runbook once Priya/Jordan confirm the prompts.

Markus Klein
Principal Engineer, Runtime Optimization
markus.klein@redwood.com
